Fucking brilliant game! Fully optimized for low end PCs and you can still see the graphics at a casual level like a charm. Fully integrated for mods, the game supports gamepads AND is a great seller when it comes to a guy who is interested in buying games like this. "Games like this?" - Ever wanted to buy a luxurious, horrific-zombie based FPS that can be turned into a comedy FPS within the click of downloading a few mods? Where you can customize the game completely externally (graphics wise) and internally with (a) (or multiple) custom texture(s), custom sounds, backgrounds, themes, GFX display, etc.

Not to mention, if you're looking for a fun fast paced FPS that allows you to play with friends then here is your train stop, and don't expect another train to come for at least 5+ months because this game with-holds endless amounts of fun.

Here is your review, from Undeadfellow. I hope it helps, and if you're looking to buy the game then I'd 100% suggest it! Enjoy!

Nearly 12 years later, this game still sets the bar for 4-player co-op PvE. Anyone who has not had the pleasure of staying up until the odd hours of the night running through the games' campaigns with friends has not truly lived; and even if you don't have a group to play with, its player-base is still pretty active! For shooter fans everywhere, this one's an essential for your Steam library.

As a player with 1,000+ hours into this game, I absolutely love it. I wish there'd be more support from Valve, but the community puts a lot of love into it, which is more than enough to keep this game alive for years to come. Even with Back 4 Blood out, this game is a masterpiece for those who love and adore co-op games like me, and is (arguably) even better than B4B. Everyone (in my opinon) should buy this game whenever it's on sale. (Usually only 1-2 USD!) It's a true classic that'll make your night.

The Last Stand Update was awesome, wish we got more content but it's fantastic. My only gripe is that it messed up a couple of mods. The game's hit-boxes still aren't the greatest at times, (especially melee) and the official servers could still use a touch up. But even with the problems, this game is an absolute blast, and I'm glad I played the living hell out of it. I hope you will too.

This game is loads of fun, if you played the console version, you'll love the Steam version.

Just avoid the toxic community.

The issue I have is some servers are very poorly hosted. Mostly ping related issues. Also, this game has the Steam Workshop available, however some texture mods can downright crash your game, or cause others to not join, unless they have the same mods installed. I don't know if it's on my end, but if you change the resolution, it will kill your game. To fix, you'll need to edit the resolution to its base resolution via files, or re-install.

Other than that, grab this game, especially when it's on sale for $1.99, like I got it.

Left 4 Dead 2 is still one of the best co-op games ever made. The gameplay is fast, chaotic, and incredibly fun, especially when playing with friends. Every run feels different thanks to the AI Director keeping things unpredictable.

The teamwork aspect is what really makes the game shine. Helping each other out, clutch saves, and barely surviving intense moments never get old. Mods and community content add even more replay value.

Even after all these years, Left 4 Dead 2 holds up amazingly well. If you enjoy co-op action, zombies, and pure fun, this game is an absolute must-play.

Cooperative game of four survivors against hordes of zombies and their special zombie counterparts. There are very subtle but genius ways the game navigates the survivors through its map design and playing as a team, as every sequence of attacks is orchestrated based on how the team is playing. A survivor caught behind, or a survivor too far ahead is punished correctly as the invisible hands of the game’s director system sees what is happening.

There is content that is carried over the entire first game’s content, survival maps, versus modes, modifiers and all sorts of room for modding/workshop as well. With all of this said, it’s a rather simple game of just shooting zombies but it’s always fun.

A semi-unrealistic run and gun FPS zombie game with a high number of fairly weak zombies that can run, climb most things, and some find you no matter where you are. There is a class of special zombies that can incapacitate you with no opportunity to recover. Needless to say teamwork is quite important and using a microphone helps.

The story line isn't very strong but there plenty of subtle clues, graffiti, and character comments that fill in some of the gaps. The characters are not nearly as compelling as L4D1 but they are all distinct and backed up by good voice acting as most Valve games are.

There are now approx. 14 official maps with the import of L4D1 maps but there are plenty of decent to good community maps to try out as well as an active modding community.

Overall a pretty good game, one of my favorites. If you've ever played a shooter and wished for more targets, this will hopefully fill that need.

The absolute peak of co-op zombie shooters!

While the first game laid a decent foundation, Left 4 Dead 2 took everything to a completely new level and perfected the formula in every imaginable way.

The gameplay is smoother, the variety of special infected, melee weapons, and campaigns is vastly superior, and the replayability is practically infinite—especially with the Steam Workshop support and all the campaigns from the first game included.

Years after its release, it remains an unmatched masterpiece of the genre and one of the best co-op experiences ever made.

10/10 – A timeless masterpiece and a must-buy!
